subject.title: feat: add Computer Use plugin manifest contract

question: Should OpenClaw accept `contracts.computerUseProviders` plus `computerUseProviderMetadata` as a stable plugin manifest contract for future macOS host permission binding now?
rationale: The new keys are public plugin API and are intended to inform a security-sensitive host-permission boundary; automation can flag the docs and code shape, but cannot choose the stable trust semantics or acceptance timing.

options.title: Accept after docs and security signoff
options.body: Regenerate the generated docs map, keep the metadata-only shape, and merge after maintainers confirm consumers will gate declarations by installed/enabled/trusted plugin state.

options.title: Defer until the host consumer lands
options.body: Hold or close this PR until the macOS host-binding implementation can review the manifest schema and trust checks together.

options.title: Narrow the contract
options.body: Keep only the provider-id contract now and postpone permission/protocol metadata until a concrete consumer proves the needed fields.

recommendation.title: Accept after docs and security signoff
recommendation.body: Regenerate the generated docs map, keep the metadata-only shape, and merge after maintainers confirm consumers will gate declarations by installed/enabled/trusted plugin state.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties `steipete` to both plugin manifest metadata and macOS onboarding/provider discovery surfaces adjacent to this decision.
